Event: `a5514e82c902b93db9e3224bcddc00b6` · 2026-10-06T04:06:23Z

> All six ruled; the brief has a dated section (.wash/local/BOOT1-implementer.md, "rulings from the early checkpoint").
> 
> Q1 yes: the milestone is the first object read, "beamlet: Elixir.Redoubt.Shell read from fsd:system", stamped.
> Q2 yes: init's [t=N] stamps only under boot-stats (the feature on redoubt-init too); every other case sees today's lines.
> Q3 yes to all three: an always-on "beamlet: at the prompt [t=N]" at the VM's first console_read (ours, not the shell's banner); userland-boot and boot-profile gain icount shift=3,sleep=off and a pinned seed, so time_now is guest time and the run repeats; the target is a regex bound on N. The icount cost is measured, not guessed: report userland-boot's wall time with and without icount on this host and raise timeout_secs only by what that needs. rv32 likewise.
> Q4 yes: counts at each power of two of requests from 2^12 (about five lines per server) plus fsd's exact counts on the sentinel walk (BootStats.x() after the 55, still not_found), under the feature only; fifteen lines do not move the boot, VOL1's 600 did.
> Q5 yes: beamlet sums guest time inside load_module/load_app and prints loads, bytes, time-in-loads, time-since-start at the prompt; the remainder is apportioned by milestone gaps (servers; VM start; parsing + console), and the report says which gap the caches can touch.
> Q6 granted: the two case files with features=["boot-stats"] and tests/data/boot-profile/{manifest-unverified.json, userland-unverified.toml} join the owned paths.

### Orchestrator · Progress

Event: `98d83c987d71fe67a633cccc8dbfd675` · 2026-10-06T05:45:39Z

> Q3 refinement ruled by the orchestrator (your 'icount cost is measured' clause decided it): `icount = shift=3,sleep=off` cannot boot the image: an idle guest's clock jumps to the next deadline, which while blkd waits on the host's virtio completion is blkd's own 10 s REQUEST_TIMEOUT_US, so the read fails and fsd:system goes corrupt; no existing icount case has a disk. So boot-profile and userland-boot use shift=3 with sleep ON (guest time is instruction time while busy, real time while idle); the run no longer repeats exactly, and the target carries the 1..5 sweep's spread; deterministic disk I/O is a separate bench package if the spread is too wide. First verified preview (rv64, seed 1): beamlet started 0.83 s, first object 10.84 s, prompt 1016.7 s guest; 999.3 s of the 1005.9 s after platform start are inside 96 loads (1.9 MB); fsd: 652 9P ops cost 77,710 littlefs reads, 25,040 of them whole-block METADATA fetches (a linear walk of ~46 metadata blocks per walk/open/read), ~2,000 CTZ pointer reads, 612 data pieces, 673 distinct blocks: directory lookup dominates, not the CTZ re-walk. EROFS1's sorted dirents are exactly the fix; please check EROFS1's brief says its profile target is set against this baseline.
